newsitem.title: USA: Stocks take lead from technology shares.
newsitem.headline: Stocks take lead from technology shares.

text.p: Stocks were lower Monday as the market took its lead from technology shares after 3Com Corp., the nation's second biggest maker of computer networking equipment, said its earnings would fall short of analysts' expectations.
At 1 p.m., the Dow Jones industrial average was off 1.54 at 6,854.26. The Nasdaq Composite index, heavily weighted with high technology issues, fell 9.34 points to 1,348.37.
In the broader market, declining issues led advances by a small margin on volume of about 266 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.

"You have the second biggest company in the networking sector, 3Com, guide analysts downward," said Larry Wachtel, an analyst at Prudential Securities. "A while ago, you had Cascade Communications and Shiva Corp. guide them lower as well. You can't beat up on all these stocks and say that everything is okay with the networking industry. Obviously, it's not."
Cascade was down 1-15/16 at 34-7/8 while Shiva fell 5/8 to 16-1/8.
Cisco Systems Inc., the biggest of the nation's networking companies, was down 4-1/8 at 59.

"The interest in this group has been enormous," Wachtel said. "A lot of people all sat in the same boat and made all kinds of money, and when you make this kind of money you put yourself in the hands of momentum traders. Once the group falters, they are gone. That is what is happening now, everyone is leaving the ship."
Dean Witter's Chief Investment Strategist, Peter Canelo said the sector would continue to do well despite the sell-off but that the stocks had their work cut out for them.

"The whole area is one that will continue to do well as demand for Internet and local area networks both continue to grow," he said. "Cisco and 3Com are both showing good export performance as international demand for American technology is boosting network equipment sales."
"They will have to work a little to stabilise and come back. Our belief is that Cisco's earnings prospects remain terrific," Canelo said.

Among blue-chip stocks that took a pounding, International Business Machines Corp. fell 3-1/2 to 145-1/4. Cowen & Co. said it cut its earnings estimates for 1997 and 1998 based on the impact of a strong dollar on the giant computer maker's sales.

Identix Inc. rose 2 to 12-5/8 after Oracle Corp. said it would use fingerprinting identification verification systems made by Identix in the next release of its Oracle Universal Server. Oracle was up 3/4 at 40-3/4.
